title: Degradation Simulation Lab and Benchmarking Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the Degradation Simulation Lab (DegradLab): an automated, repeatable harness for injecting controlled resource and behavioral degradation into Redwood Inference stack components to validate SLO resilience, fallback correctness, and cost/quality tradeoffs before deployments. It codifies scenarios, instrumentation requirements, pass/fail criteria, and an owner-run checklist for both feature rollouts and model/quantization changes.

Goals:
- Provide reproducible degradation scenarios that exercise latency, throughput, cache-staleness, and model-fidelity fallbacks.
- Surface regressions in end-to-end latency SLOs and quality regressions tied to degraded paths (quantization, fallback variants).
- Standardize acceptance criteria for production rollouts and model promotions.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: API gateway, edge routing, runtime serving tier (GPU pools), KV/prefix cache, model variant fallback, telemetry pipeline.
- Out-of-scope: third-party infra outside Redwood control (cloud provider control plane).

Key concepts:
1) Degradation modes:
  - Resource contention (CPU/GPU throttling, memory pressure)
  - Network degradation (increased egress latency, packet loss emulation)
  - Service slow-downs (artificial request processing delay)
  - Cache staleness (prefix/KV cache eviction and cold-hit ratios)
  - Model fidelity shift (downgrading from full-precision to quantized variant)
2) Fidelity tiers and fallbacks:
  - Tier 0: Default model (highest-quality)
  - Tier 1: Quantized/fast variant with verified quality budget
  - Tier 2: Small-context or summary fallback (reduced cost/latency)

DegradLab architecture (logical):
- Experiment controller (k8s job with declarative JSON experiment manifests)
- Synthetic traffic generator (workload profiles: chat-heavy, short-gen, embedding-batch)
- Failure injectors (chaos proxy for network, cgroups-based CPU/GPU throttler, cache warm/cold driver)
- Telemetry collector (aggregates traces, histograms, error rates to the observability cluster)
- Analysis engine (computes SLO deltas, regression alerts, and artifact storage)

Standard scenarios (examples):
1) Cold-cache burst: 5-minute warmdown; then ramp 200 rps for 10 minutes with cache disabled. Pass if p95 latency <= 2x baseline and error rate < 0.2%.
2) Quantization fallback under GPU pressure: throttle 40% GPU cycles on 20% of shards and observe automatic quantized variant routing. Pass if output-churn is within 1% of baseline accuracy for labeled prompt set and tail latency SLOs hold.
3) Out-of-region failover: simulate region 1 routing drop; verify routing to nearest region, tokens-per-second degradation <= 30% and no more than 1% client-facing errors.
4) Streaming slow-path: inject 500ms additional per-chunk processing for streaming endpoints; pass if partial-result checkpoints resume without user-visible corruption and retry logic recovers within configured window.

Metric mapping and thresholds (excerpt):
| Metric | SLO | Alert threshold | Analysis window |
| p50 latency (ms) | baseline+10% | >= baseline+40% | 5m |
| p95 latency (ms) | baseline+50% | >= baseline+100% | 5m |
| request_error_rate | <= 0.5% | >= 1% | 5m |
| model-quality-regression | delta F1 <= 0.01 | delta F1 >= 0.03 | experiment run |

Experiment manifest (short example):
{
  "name": "quant-fallback-under-gpu-pressure-2026-06",
  "duration": "15m",
  "traffic_profile": "chat-heavy-200rps",
  "injectors": ["gpu-throttle:40%:shard=odd", "cache-evict:100%:namespace=prefix-store"],
  "quality_checks": ["evalset:release-candidate-prompts", "threshold:delta-f1<=0.01"]
}

How to run (operator steps):
1) Create experiment manifest in /infra/experiments/ and open PR referencing the target rollout.
2) Start a dry-run in staging: kubectl apply -f degradlab/experiment-job.yaml --namespace=staging. Monitor logs: kubectl logs -f job/degradlab-controller.
3) Verify baseline collection and artifact upload to s3://redwood-degradlab-results/<run-id>.
4) If artifacts pass local quality gates, schedule a controlled run in canary environment with traffic mirroring.
5) Report: attach autogenerated PDF summary to the rollout ticket and notify owners.

Acceptance checklist for releases (must be completed before gated rollout):
- [ ] Relevant scenarios executed for the change type (code, model, infra).
- [ ] No metric exceeded alert threshold for >5m during run, or documented mitigation.
- [ ] Model-quality regression within defined budget on the canonical evalset.
- [ ] Artifacts stored and linked on the release PR.
- [ ] Rollback plan documented with exact version IDs.

Dashboards and alerts required (minimum):
- DegradLab overview (run state, pass/fail, run-id)
- Latency heatmap per service over the experiment window
- Model-quality delta panel with prompt-level breakout
- Experiment-run SLO delta and incident indicator (auto-open if alert threshold crossed)

Ownership and cadence:
- Owner: runtime-performance team (primary), eng-sre (on-call escalation).
- Monthly automated regression runs against the default model catalog.
- Ad-hoc runs required for any quantization change, runtime kernel update, or routing policy change.

Decision record summary (ADR required):
- This playbook implements ADR-PRE-23: experiments are mandatory for any production change that could alter per-token latency or model fidelity beyond defined budgets. The ADR mandates storing run artifacts for 90 days and attaching the run-id to the release.

Appendix: common CLI snippets
# launch local experiment against staging cluster
make degradlab-run EXPERIMENT=./manifests/quant-fallback.json TARGET=staging

# download run artifacts
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-degradlab-results/<run-id>/summary.json ./ --profile redwood-admin

Notes and follow-ups:
- Add a dedicated synthetic embedding workload to the catalog (action: runtime-performance, due 2026-07-01).
- Integrate artifact provenance signature to meet compliance for Private deployments (action: security-and-compliance).

Related artifacts:

- canonical evalset: evalsets/release-candidate-2026.json

If you are implementing a new quantization or routing policy and have questions about which scenarios to run, ping the reviewers listed on this page before starting the experiment.
